text.p: These are the leading stories in. the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Mubarak and (ex-Israeli prime minister) Peres hold constructive talks in Sharm el-Sheikh to support the peace process. The president: the peace process is not dead but it needs reviving and the peoples of the region want development.

- Twelve storey-building collapses on top of its residents in a catastrophic accident in Heliopolis. Rescue workers find nine bodies, 17 injured and are searching for more than 150 beneath the rubble. Storeys were erected illegally on top of the ill-fated building.

- Mubarak after his discussions with Peres: the peoples of the region want peace for the sake of development. Rabin and Peres have made brave and exemplary efforts to progress the Palestinian issue. President tours Sharm el-Sheikh.
- Two dead, 12 injured and 17 saved after a building collapses in Heliopolis. Mubarak is following up the situation.
- Government to allocate 3.5 billion pounds to fund textile firms buying cotton this year.
- Thirteen-storey building collapses in Heliopolis. Three bodies, 18 injured and the search continues.
- Mubarak says the peace process needs energising.
- Egypt scraps sales tax on gold bars, raises sales taxes on some cars by 15 percent.
- After 14 years and three children.. husband realises he is impotent and that wife conceived children from his friends.
